Main goal: To compute the length of the longest bitonic subsequence in an integer array—i.e., a subsequence that first strictly increases and then strictly decreases.

Summary:
This code uses dynamic programming in two passes. First, it computes lis[i], the length of the longest increasing subsequence ending at index i. Finally, it finds the maximum value of (lis[i] + lds[i] - 1) over all i, which represents the length of the longest bitonic subsequence.

Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Checking for a Subsequence with Sum Divisible by m

Main Goal:
Determine if there exists a non-empty subset of the input array whose sum is congruent to 0 modulo m.

Description:
The function modularSum(int[] arr, int n, int m) uses a boolean DP array of size m to track which residues modulo m can be formed by subsets of the first i elements. It iterates through the array, updating reachable residues by adding the current element’s value (mod m) to previously reachable residues. If at any point residue 0 becomes reachable, or if n > m (by the pigeonhole principle a subset sum must be 0 mod m), it returns true. Otherwise, after processing all elements, it returns whether residue 0 is reachable.

mbpp_0747.reference_description: Write a function to find the longest common subsequence for the given three string sequence.

Description_Simple.comparison_text: This code defines a method `lcsOfThree` that takes three strings X, Y, Z and builds a 3D DP table `L` sized (m+1)×(n+1)×(o+1), where m, n, o are their lengths. mbpp_0469.reference_description: Write a function to find the maximum profit earned from a maximum of k stock transactions

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find the maximum profit earned from a maximum of k stock transactions
Description_Simple.comparison_text: This code implements a dynamic programming solution to the classic “stock buy-and-sell with at most k transactions” problem. It builds a table finalProfit[i][j] that records the maximum profit achievable using up to i transactions in the first j+1 days. For each transaction count i and day j, it considers either skipping the j-th day (carrying over finalProfit[i][j-1]) or selling on day j after a previous buy on some day x (price[j] – price[x] + finalProfit[i-1][x]), taking the maximum of these options. The answer is finalProfit[k][n-1], the best profit using up to k transactions over all days.

Title: Max Sum Without Three Consecutive Elements

Main Goal: Given an integer array, this code computes the maximum possible sum of its elements under the constraint that you cannot select three consecutive elements.

How It Works:
1. It builds a DP array `sum[]` where `sum[i]` stores the best sum using elements up to index `i` without ever taking three in a row.
2. Base cases:
   - `sum[0] = arr[0]`
   - `sum[1] = arr[0] + arr[1]`
   - `sum[2]` is the maximum of either skipping one of the first three or taking any two of them.
3. Recurrence for `i ≥ 3`:
   - Skip `arr[i]`: carry over `sum[i-1]`
   - Take `arr[i]` but skip `arr[i-1]`: `sum[i-2] + arr[i]`

Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Count Number of Ways to Paint Fence Posts with k Colors

Main Goal:
This code computes, for n fence posts and k available colors, the total number of ways to paint the posts so that no more than two adjacent posts share the same color. It uses dynamic programming with the recurrence:
  dp[1] = k
  dp[2] = k * k
  dp[i] = (k−1) * (dp[i−1] + dp[i−2]) mod 1e9+7
to build up the solution efficiently under modular arithmetic.

Title: LeftInsertion – Compute Lower Bound Insertion Index

Main goal: This code implements a binary search to find the leftmost (first) position at which a value x can be inserted into a sorted array a so that the array remains sorted. It returns the smallest index i where all elements before i are strictly less than x and all elements from i onward are ≥ x.

How it works:
- Initialize search bounds lo = 0, hi = a.length.
- Repeatedly compute mid = lo + (hi – lo)/2.
- If a[mid] < x, narrow the search to the right half (lo = mid + 1); otherwise, search the left half (hi = mid).
- Loop until lo == hi, at which point lo is the correct insertion index.
- Runs in O(log n) time.

Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: BitUtils.countUnsetBits

Main Goal: This function counts how many bits in the binary representation of a given non-negative integer n are zero (unset) from the least significant bit up to the highest bit that could be set in n.

How It Works:
- Initialize a mask x at 1 (the least significant bit).
- Loop while x is no greater than n.
- In each iteration, use a bitwise AND (x & n). If the result is zero, that bit in n is unset, so increment the count.
- Left-shift x by one to move to the next bit.
- Return the total count of unset bits.

Title: Toggle First and Last Set Bits

Main Goal:
This code flips (toggles) the most significant and least significant ‘1’ bits in the binary representation of a positive integer.

How it works:
1. takeLAndFSetBits(n):  
   - Propagates the highest set bit to all lower positions (using successive ORs with right-shifts).  
   - After propagation, n becomes a sequence of 1s from the MSB down to bit 0.  
   - It then computes ((n+1)>>1)+1, which yields a mask having just two 1’s: one at the original MSB and one at the original LSB.

2. toggleFAndLBits(n):  
   - Calls takeLAndFSetBits(n) to get the two-bit mask.  
   - Returns n XOR mask, thereby flipping only the first (MSB) and last (LSB) set bits of n.

Main Goal: To reorder a list of integers so that all positive numbers (sorted ascending) come first, then zeros, and finally negative numbers (also sorted ascending), using a single stream-based sort with a custom comparator.
